newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher, profit-taking trims gains.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher, profit-taking trims gains.

text.p: Share prices stayed in positive territory until the close although profit-taking emerged in the afternoon to shave part of earlier gains.
"People are cautious as budget day draws nearer," said a TA Securities dealer. "Though the budget is expected to be positive, players are not willing are carry large positions into Friday."
Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim will present the 1997 budget in parliament on Friday.
Dealers said Second Board stocks continued to dominate interest while selective buying by funds kept blue chips steady.
The Second Board index closed up 4.75 points at 629.85 after hitting the day's high of 633.81, just short of its all-time record of 635.84 set on Monday.
The blue-chip focused Composite Index ended at 1,178.35, up 2.37 points.
An analyst said that though a market-friendly budget would limit the downside, a surge beyond 1,200 is unlikely given the current fair valuation of the market.
"Funds are in the market but they have not been aggressive. So I don't think the market can break 1,200 this year," he said.
